issues.description: Email regex validation is overly permissive and may accept invalid email addresses (e.g., 'test@domain' without proper TLD validation)
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation library like 'validator.js' or implement stricter regex pattern. Consider: /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is incomplete for comprehensive XSS prevention. Missing encoding for other special characters and doesn't handle all attack vectors
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify or implement a comprehensive encoding function that handles all HTML contexts. Current approach only handles basic cases and may miss template literal injections or attribute-based XSS

issues.description: Missing JSDoc documentation for return type and parameters
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc with @param and @returns tags: '@param {CreateUserInput} input - The user creation input\n@returns {Promise<User>} The created user object'

issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and may produce collisions at scale
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for Node.js (v14.17+) or the 'uuid' package. Example: 'import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; return randomUUID();' or use a proper ID generation strategy with database sequences

issues.description: Date.now() combined with Math.random() in ID generation may cause collisions if multiple users are created in rapid succession
issues.suggestion: Replace with crypto.randomUUID() or use a distributed ID generation system like Snowflake IDs or UUIDs from a dedicated library

issues.description: Email is converted to lowercase but not trimmed, allowing whitespace manipulation
issues.suggestion: Add .trim() before .toLowerCase() to prevent whitespace-based bypass: 'email: input.email.trim().toLowerCase()'

issues.description: Generic error messages may not provide sufficient context for debugging or user feedback
issues.suggestion: Use custom error classes with error codes for better error handling. Example: 'throw new ValidationError('EMAIL_REQUIRED', 'Email and name are required')'

issues.description: Email sanitization is not performed, only the name field is sanitized
issues.suggestion: Consider adding email normalization/validation beyond just lowercase conversion. Validate against email injection patterns if the email will be used in email headers

issues.description: Database query is commented out, making this code non-functional in production. No error handling for database operations
issues.suggestion: Uncomment and implement actual database connection with proper error handling, connection pooling, and transaction support. Add try-catch block and log errors appropriately

issues.description: No validation for input string length before sanitization, could cause performance issues with extremely large inputs
issues.suggestion: Add length validation before processing: 'if (input.name.length > 1000) throw new Error('Name too long');' Adjust limit based on business requirements

issues.description: User interface uses Date object which may cause serialization issues when converting to JSON
issues.suggestion: Consider using ISO string format (string type) for createdAt field to ensure consistent serialization across different environments and databases

issues.description: No rate limiting or timing attack prevention in validation logic
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting for user creation endpoint to prevent enumeration attacks and abuse. Consider using constant-time comparison for sensitive operations

codeQuality.summary: This code demonstrates good security awareness with parameterized queries, input validation, and XSS prevention attempts. However, it has several medium-severity issues: (1) weak ID generation using Math.random() instead of cryptographically secure methods, (2) incomplete email validation regex, (3) basic HTML encoding that may miss certain XSS vectors, and (4) commented-out database code with no error handling. The code shows good structure and intent but needs hardening for production use. Main improvements needed: use crypto.randomUUID(), implement comprehensive input sanitization with established libraries, add proper error handling, and trim email inputs. No critical security vulnerabilities were found, but the medium-severity issues could lead to bugs or security problems at scale.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is a security-critical function that guards user input. Invalid regex patterns or edge cases could allow malformed emails into the system, leading to downstream failures or security vulnerabilities.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: 'should accept valid standard email' - Input: isValidEmail('user@example.com') - Expected: true. Test: 'should reject email without @ symbol' - Input: isValidEmail('usergmail.com') - Expected: false. Test: 'should reject email without TLD' - Input: isValidEmail('user@domain') - Expected: false (current implementation incorrectly returns true). Test: 'should reject email with spaces' - Input: isValidEmail('user @example.com') - Expected: false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation must handle empty strings and edge cases. The function does not explicitly check for empty input, which could lead to unexpected behavior or security bypasses.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: 'should reject empty string' - Input: isValidEmail('') - Expected: false. Test: 'should reject multiple @ symbols' - Input: isValidEmail('user@@example.com') - Expected: false (current regex may allow this). Test: 'should reject consecutive dots in domain' - Input: isValidEmail('user@example..com') - Expected: false. Test: 'should reject email starting with @' - Input: isValidEmail('@example.com') - Expected: false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: XSS prevention is critical for security. Inadequate sanitization could allow malicious scripts to execute in user browsers, leading to data theft, session hijacking, or account compromise.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: 'should escape script tag' - Input: sanitizeInput('<script>alert(1)</script>') - Expected: '<script>alert(1)</script>'. Test: 'should escape double quotes' - Input: sanitizeInput('value="dangerous"') - Expected: 'value="dangerous"'. Test: 'should escape single quotes' - Input: sanitizeInput("It's here") - Expected: 'It's here'. Test: 'should escape all dangerous characters' - Input: sanitizeInput('<>\'"') - Expected: '<>'"'.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Sanitization function lacks null/undefined checks. Passing null or undefined will cause runtime TypeError when calling .replace(). Also needs to handle empty strings, Unicode, and already-escaped content.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: 'should handle empty string' - Input: sanitizeInput('') - Expected: ''. Test: 'should preserve Unicode characters' - Input: sanitizeInput('José María 日本語') - Expected: 'José María 日本語' (unchanged). Test: 'should handle mixed dangerous and safe content' - Input: sanitizeInput('Name: <tag>José</tag>') - Expected: 'Name: <tag>José</tag>'. Test: 'should handle ampersand' - Input: sanitizeInput('A&B') - Expected: document behavior (currently not escaped, should be '&').

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email should be normalized to lowercase to prevent duplicate accounts with different casing (User@Example.com vs user@example.com). This is essential for data integrity.

untestedPaths.reasoning: ID generation must produce unique identifiers. Collisions could cause database constraint violations or data corruption. The weak randomness (Math.random()) and predictable timestamp make IDs guessable.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: 'should generate ID with correct format' - Input: const id = generateId() - Expected: id matches pattern /^user_\d+_[a-z0-9]{7}$/. Test: 'should generate unique IDs on repeated calls' - Input: const ids = Array.from({length: 1000}, () => generateId()); const uniqueIds = new Set(ids) - Expected: uniqueIds.size === 1000 (no collisions). Test: 'should include timestamp in ID' - Input: const before = Date.now(); const id = generateId(); const after = Date.now(); const timestamp = parseInt(id.split('_')[1]) - Expected: timestamp >= before && timestamp <= after.

This is a security-critical module containing email validation, XSS sanitization, and user creation logic. CRITICAL gaps: (1) isValidEmail function lacks tests for valid/invalid formats, empty strings, multiple @ symbols, and edge cases - current regex is overly permissive. (2) sanitizeInput function has no tests for XSS prevention, null/undefined handling, or Unicode characters - missing ampersand escaping. (3) createUser function lacks tests for happy path, all error branches (missing email/name, invalid format), XSS sanitization verification, and email normalization. (4) generateId lacks uniqueness tests and uses weak randomness (Math.random()). (5) saveUser has no tests for parameter formatting or error handling. (6) Missing tests for whitespace-only inputs, database failures, and concurrent access. RECOMMENDATIONS: Create fixtures/clean-code.test.ts with 20+ test cases covering: isValidEmail (10 cases for valid/invalid formats), sanitizeInput (8 cases for XSS vectors and edge cases), createUser (12 cases for happy path, error branches, sanitization integration), generateId (uniqueness and format), and saveUser (parameter handling and mocked database calls). Priority: CRITICAL - this code handles user input and security validations without any test safety net.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive test coverage for security-critical functions. The file has 0% test coverage with no test files found. Create fixtures/clean-code.test.ts with 20+ test cases covering isValidEmail, sanitizeInput, createUser, generateId, and saveUser functions.

Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() for ID generation. Current implementation is not cryptographically secure and may produce collisions at scale, potentially causing database constraint violations or security issues.

Enhance email validation with a more robust regex or use a well-tested library like 'validator.js'. Current regex is overly permissive and may accept invalid emails (e.g., 'test@domain' without proper TLD validation).

Improve XSS sanitization by using a comprehensive library like DOMPurify or implementing complete HTML entity encoding. Current implementation only handles basic cases and misses ampersand encoding, potentially leaving XSS vulnerabilities.

Implement actual database connection with proper error handling. The database query is currently commented out, making the code non-functional. Add try-catch blocks, connection pooling, and transaction support.

Add .trim() to email processing to prevent whitespace-based bypass. Email is converted to lowercase but not trimmed, allowing whitespace manipulation that could bypass duplicate checks.

Create custom error classes with error codes for better programmatic error handling. Replace generic Error messages with structured ValidationError types that include field names and machine-readable error codes.
